answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence shared decisions, then cap the weight of any one stake-bearing account. A new identity gains no extra influence unless the attacker locks up more capital, while coordination rules can slash stakes for provable duplicate claims or abuse. For example, a zephyr-themed bot on a mesa marketplace still needs its own bonded deposit; wrapping that claim in a cipher does not erase the on-chain cost or make the stake reusable elsewhere.
